intent: A release veto for product truth and premium experience. Aggregate quality can never compensate for a critical failure.

anchors.1.0: Release-grade: complete, independently evidenced, and robust under adverse cases.
anchors.0.9: Strong: only minor, non-load-bearing polish gaps remain.
anchors.0.75: Material weakness: credible work exists, but the dimension is not release-grade.
anchors.0.5: Prototype quality: important paths or qualities are incomplete.

protocol_truth.release_grade: Native document.modelContext behavior, honest origin/lifecycle state, evidence-only publisher tools, and agent-side derivation are proved in the target browser.

evidence_integrity.release_grade: Every consequential claim resolves to immutable, current-source evidence with provenance; unknowns and blocked checks remain explicit.

functional_completeness.release_grade: The clean-session golden workflow, confirmation/rejection, persistence, reset, errors, and agent-free human path all work end to end.

visual_direction.release_grade: The rendered product has a distinct editorial system, intentional typography, depth, hierarchy, and Semantic Focus Shift; it does not read as generic HTML or a routine dashboard.

interaction_motion_quality.release_grade: All important controls expose hover, pressed, focus, loading, empty, error, and transition states; motion explains state and remains smooth and reversible.

accessibility_responsiveness.release_grade: Keyboard, focus, semantics, contrast, reduced motion, and representative mobile/tablet/desktop layouts preserve the complete task without clipping or hidden controls.

regression_safety.release_grade: Unit, integration, negative-path, build, type, and targeted visual checks protect the golden path and fail when load-bearing behavior is removed.

release_reproducibility.release_grade: A clean public checkout and deployed target-client session reproduce the verified result using complete instructions, pinned artifacts, and an auditable release identity.

automatic_failures.native_protocol_bypass: Any silent WebMCP polyfill, direct-call demo fallback, publisher-side conclusion, or hardcoded tool-name coupling.
automatic_failures.false_or_stale_evidence: Any release claim backed by missing, contradictory, fabricated, stale-source, or wrong-environment evidence.
automatic_failures.incomplete_golden_workflow: Any load-bearing golden-path step is absent, operator-faked, non-reproducible, or reports success after failure.
automatic_failures.generic_html_dashboard_quality: Independent desktop and mobile review finds the product reads as ordinary HTML/admin UI: weak hierarchy plus routine card/sidebar structure plus absent distinctive depth, typography, or semantic transformation. Three or more of those pattern clusters trigger this veto.
automatic_failures.decorative_or_inaccessible_motion: Motion obscures state, breaks reduced-motion meaning, causes unreachable controls, or animates layout properties on a load-bearing interaction.
automatic_failures.critical_accessibility_failure: The golden task cannot be completed by keyboard, focus becomes lost/hidden, meaningful content lacks semantics, or a representative viewport clips an essential control.
automatic_failures.regression_or_build_failure: A required test/type/build/negative-path check fails, or a known load-bearing regression has no protective test.
automatic_failures.non_reproducible_release: The public release cannot be reproduced from a clean checkout/session, or shipped source/artifacts differ from evaluated identity.
automatic_failures.unreviewed_high_stakes_judgment: A qualitative critical-dimension score lacks independent rendered-product review and attached evidence.
